bullets: How percent means out of one hundred, and how to find 25% of 60 by seeing it as one quarter of the whole
slides.heading: Percentage: 25% of 60
slides.notes: Welcome everyone in and say: today we work with percent - what 25% really means, and how to find 25% of 60 - and by the end you will be able to explain why the answer is not 25.

bullets: Read a percent as a count out of one hundred: 25% is 25 out of 100
See 25% as one quarter of the whole
Find 25% of 60 by dividing the whole into quarters: 60 / 4 = 15
slides.heading: What we will learn
slides.notes: Read the three goals aloud and tell the class: keep these in mind, because the exit ticket at the end will ask you to do exactly these things.

bullets: A classmate says 25% of 60 is just 25 - after all, the question says 25
Is that right? What does the 25 in 25% really count?
slides.heading: Is 25% of 60 just 25?
slides.notes: Ask for a show of hands: is 25% of 60 equal to 25, or something else? Take two or three answers without judging them yet; say: hold on to your idea, because scene s2 settles this exactly.

bullets: A percent counts out of one hundred: 25% is 25 out of every 100, not the plain number 25
The whole matters: here the whole is 60, so the answer is a share of 60
slides.heading: A percent is a share of a whole
slides.notes: Say this slowly, because it is the big idea of the whole lesson: the number in a percent counts out of one hundred, and the answer is always a share of the whole in the question.

bullets: On the hundred-grid, shade twenty-five cells out of one hundred - that shaded amount is 25%
25% is 25 out of 100: a rate per hundred, whatever the whole turns out to be
slides.heading: Percent means per hundred
slides.notes: Point at the grid as the cells shade in and narrate: each cell is one out of one hundred, and twenty-five of them make 25 percent.

bullets: Careful - the trap is: 25% of 60 is just 25.
The 25 counts out of one hundred, and the whole here is 60 - so the answer must be a share of 60, not 25 itself
slides.heading: Watch out: 25% is not just 25
slides.notes: Hold the claim up against the grid: the 25 belongs to the hundred, and our whole is 60, so answering 25 mixes up two different wholes.

bullets: 25 out of 100 simplifies to one quarter, so 25% of 60 is one quarter of 60
Split 60 into four equal parts: 60 / 4 = 15, so 25% of 60 is 15
slides.heading: 25% of 60: divide into quarters
slides.notes: Narrate the split slowly: one quarter means four equal parts, and each part of 60 is 15. The answer is 15.

bullets: A percent is out of one hundred, so first turn it into a fraction of the whole
25% of 60 is 15, because 25% means one quarter of the whole
slides.heading: The takeaway
slides.notes: Land the whole chain in one breath: per hundred, then one quarter, then divide the whole into quarters - 25% of 60 is 15.

bullets: Work 25% of 60 in two steps: first write 25% as one quarter, then divide the whole into quarters
60 / 4 = 15 - check by rebuilding: four quarters of 15 make 60 again
slides.heading: Worked example: 25% of 60
slides.notes: Talk through the two steps slowly as in scene s3 and name each one as you write it; say: turning the percent into a fraction of the whole first keeps the working honest.

bullets: What is 50% of 60? Use the same idea: 50% is one half of the whole
Careful - a classmate says: 25% of 60 is just 25. Correct them in one sentence, naming what the 25 really counts
slides.heading: Your turn: find a percent of a quantity
slides.notes: Give pairs three minutes, then cold-call one pair on each part: press them on the fraction step first, then on the exact sentence they used to correct the claim.

bullets: On your own: work out 25% of 60, showing the quarter step
Watch out for the trap one last time: 25% of 60 is just 25. Say what 25% of 60 really is, and why
slides.heading: Exit ticket: show what you know
slides.notes: Collect these before anyone leaves and say: I am looking for the quarter step in your first answer, plus one clear sentence about per hundred in your second.
